content_html:
Air fryers have moved from novelty appliance to everyday kitchen equipment for many households. The best model for you depends less on the number of presets and more on capacity, drawer layout, worktop space and how often you will actually use it.

For this 2026 guide, we reviewed current independent UK testing and focused on models that stand out for different types of buyer. We have not carried out our own laboratory testing, so use this as a shortlist to compare and check the latest specifications, warranty and owner feedback before buying.

1. Ninja Double Stack XL SL400UK - strong all-round family option

Good Food currently highlights the Ninja Double Stack XL SL400UK as its best overall air fryer. Its two 4.75-litre drawers are stacked vertically rather than side by side, giving a large 9.5-litre total capacity without making the appliance unusually wide.

It is particularly appealing for families or anyone who wants to cook two foods at once. The trade-off is height and noise, so it is worth measuring the gap below your wall cupboards before ordering.

2. Ninja Foodi MAX Dual Zone - useful for bigger households

Good Food has also rated the large Ninja Foodi MAX Dual Zone highly for family cooking. Separate drawers can run at different temperatures and the sync function allows them to finish together.

This type of dual-drawer air fryer is useful when you regularly cook a main item and side dish at the same time, but it takes up more worktop space than a compact single-basket model.

Compare Ninja Foodi MAX Dual Zone listings on eBay UK

3. Ninja Crispi 4-in-1 - compact and versatile glass-bowl design

Good Food awarded the Ninja Crispi 4-in-1 strong marks for versatility. Its glass cooking containers can also be used for storage, which gives it a different feel from a conventional drawer air fryer.

It makes particular sense for smaller portions, leftovers and buyers who like being able to see the food while it cooks. If you regularly cook large family batches, a bigger dual-drawer model may be more practical.

Compare Ninja Crispi 4-in-1 listings on eBay UK

4. Cosori Air Fryer Lite 3.8L - smaller-capacity option

Good Food has highlighted the Cosori Air Fryer Lite 3.8L as a useful compact choice. Its smaller capacity is better suited to one or two people than a large family, while its straightforward design helps keep the footprint manageable.

If space is limited, comparing a smaller single-basket model against a large dual-zone fryer can save both money and valuable counter space.

Compare Cosori Air Fryer Lite 3.8L listings on eBay UK

What to look for before buying an air fryer

Capacity: A larger litre figure is useful only if the basket layout works for the meals you cook. Two drawers can be more flexible than one very large basket.

Footprint: Check width, depth and height. Tall stacked models can save width but may sit close to low cupboards.

Cleaning: Removable dishwasher-safe baskets and trays make frequent use much easier.

Power and cooking zones: Dual-zone models are convenient but often use more power when both zones are running.

Useful functions: Air fry, roast, reheat and bake are often more valuable than a long list of novelty presets.

Which one should you compare first?

For a larger household, the Ninja Double Stack XL and Foodi MAX Dual Zone are sensible starting points. For smaller kitchens or portions, the Cosori Lite is easier to accommodate, while the Ninja Crispi offers a more unusual glass-container design.

Prices, offers and availability change regularly. Always check the live listing, warranty, dimensions and returns policy before purchasing.
